Title: Introducing Granular: The Agentic Terminal for Non-Developers
# Introducing Granular: The Agentic Terminal for Non-Developers. Introducing Granular: One agentic terminal app to replace the chaos of working with AI agents. Plug in the Claude, Codex, and Gemini subscriptions you already pay for, point a whole team of agents at any project folder on your machine, and build anything with zero coding skills. In this video you will learn how to:. → Run Claude, Codex, and Gemini from one app and switch accounts on the fly. → Point a whole team of agents at any project folder and build locally, no lock-in. → Appoint a boss agent that spawns its own workers to split the job. → Install a "brain" that gives your agents a self-moving roadmap and shared living memory. → Lock your API keys in an encrypted vault your agents can actually use safely. → Preview, annotate, commit, and publish in plain English, even from your phone. Here's the shift: IDEs like VS Code and Cursor were never built for agentic workflows for non developer... Granular is built from the ground up for non-technical builders: founders, designers, marketers, PMs. This is the app I wish I had when I started building with AI six months ago... 🖥️ Try Granular (free plan — 2 projects, 4 sessions each, no tool restrictions): https://granular.build/go/intro. 🛠️ [01:37] What can it do? And the cherry on top of all of this is that you can build and run all of it right from your phone.

Build me a landing page for early access and publish it. [...] Where does my work live?

On your Mac, as plain files under real git. Keys and tokens sit in an encrypted local vault and are injected only when a tool needs them. Push to GitHub whenever you like; every bit of it is yours.

 What do I need, and what's not here yet?

A Mac with Apple Silicon. Windows isn't here yet (join the Windows waitlist), and Gemini support is still landing. There is a phone bridge over Telegram to keep an eye on your agents from anywhere, but Granular itself is Mac-first.

 Is Granular available on Windows yet?

Yes. Granular runs on Mac (Apple Silicon) and on Windows. Windows is in beta and gets every update the same day as Mac. Download for Mac or Windows.
